What We’ve Learned Since 9/11
A quarter-century ago, our world changed. The terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon shattered America’s sense that nothing could dent its security or station in the world. From an economic standpoint, the nation’s fiscal status has been turned upside down—from a federal budget swimming in surpluses to one deeply in deficit, despite the U.S. not being in recession or officially at war.
